podcast.title: Arrest and Departure from Coheed and Cambria (July-August 2011)
podcast.body: After the Walgreens robbery, Michael Todd was tracked down via the taxi company and arrested on charges of possession and armed robbery, held on $10,000 bail. The band's keyboard player filled in on bass for that night's show, and Todd officially left the band on August 4, 2011. "Todd left the band on August 4."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Legal Sentence and Cancer Diagnosis (Post-2011)
podcast.body: Michael Todd was sentenced to one year of home confinement and three years of probation, which included mandatory drug counseling sessions. Life became further complicated when he was diagnosed with cancer in 2012, though he later recovered and has pursued solo projects. "He was sentenced to one year's home confinement and three years of probation in order to attend drug counseling sessions."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: OxyContin Addiction and Armed Robbery (July 10, 2011)
podcast.body: As the bassist for Coheed and Cambria, Michael Todd developed an addiction to OxyContin. On July 10, 2011, during a tour stop in Mansfield, Massachusetts, he took a taxi to a Walgreens in Adelboro, where he robbed the pharmacist of six bottles of OxyContin by threatening them with a bomb via a message on his phone. "He got hooked on OxyContin."

xref.title: Band Expulsion and Sentencing
xref.body: Following his arrest, Michael Todd was immediately removed from Coheed and Cambria. At his trial, he received a sentence of one year of home confinement, three years of probation, and a requirement for extensive drug treatment. The leniency in his sentence was partly influenced by his recent diagnosis with testicular cancer. "Todd was immediately kicked out of the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Escape and Arrest
xref.body: After obtaining the drugs, Michael Todd fled the Walgreens, ran across a field behind the building, and jumped into a cab. His intention was to make that night's gig in nearby Mansfield, Massachusetts. However, security cameras at the pharmacy and witness identification of the cab company allowed authorities to track the cab to the Coheed and Cambria tour bus in the venue's parking lot, where Todd was arrested before the band took the stage. "Before the bank had hit the stage that night, Todd was arrested."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Fan Scamming and Financial Troubles
xref.body: Despite a lenient sentence for the robbery, Michael Todd later admitted to scamming fans of Coheed and Cambria. He accepted money for band merchandise that he did not actually own or possess, further contributing to his financial problems, particularly in light of his ongoing cancer treatments. "But then, he admitted to scamming fans of the band by accepting money to sell co-heat and Cambria merchandise that he didn't actually own."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Walgreens Robbery Attempt
xref.body: In July 2011, while on tour with Soundgarden, Coheed and Cambria's bass player Michael Todd was arrested for attempting to rob a Walgreens drug store in Massachusetts. He entered the store and showed the pharmacist a note on his Blackberry stating, "I have a bomb, give me some oxycontin or else." When no OxyContin was available, he demanded 30-milligram Percocets plus Oxycodone. "He was arrested for trying to rob a Walgreens drug store in Massachusetts."
